articles.title: Serie A | Como 0-0 Roma: Giallorossi resist under siege after Malen sees red
articles.summary: Roma were ultimately pleased with the first 0-0 of the Serie A season away to Como, as Donyell Malen was sent off for dangerous play, leaving them down to 10...
articles.body:
Roma were ultimately pleased with the first 0-0 of the Serie A season away to Como, as Donyell Malen was sent off for dangerous play, leaving them down to 10 men for over 30 minutes.

These sides snatched Champions League qualification from more prestigious clubs last season and were hoping to repeat it. The hosts lost Moise Kean to injury on international duty and needed to shake off the surprising 2-0 defeat to Frosinone. The Giallorossi lost Mile Svilar for at least a month to a fractured toe, so Pierluigi Gollini got his first Serie A appearance in two years, while Lorenzo Pellegrini replaced injured Bryan Cristante.

ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Cesc Fabregas, Manager of Como 1907, and Gian Piero Gasperini, Manager of AS Roma, embrace before the Serie A match between Como 1907 and AS Roma at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Paulo Dybala scuffed a finish straight at Jean Butez after a Donyell Malen knockdown, then Gollini rushed off his line to close down Nico Paz at the near post, but Pellegrini came closest with a strike thumping the base of the upright from the edge of the area on 11 minutes.

Gianluca Mancini's scuffed clearance after an awkward bounce allowed Maxence Caqueret to drill inches wide, then Malen flicked a long Pellegrini ball around Butez, but the angle was too narrow to score.

Gollini made just one appearance last season for Roma in the Europa League, but didn't seem rusty as he rushed out to smother at the feet of Caqueret on a Yan Couto through ball.

ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Wesley of AS Roma is challenged by Assane Diao of Como 1907 during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and AS Roma at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

On the stroke of half-time, Wesley clipped Assane Diao's heel as he was running towards goal, but the referee waved play on and only booked the Como player for dissent, much to the incredulity of Cesc Fabregas. It was an extremely risky situation, but Evan Ndicka's presence perhaps rescued Wesley from a VAR intervention.

The referee was involved again after the restart, because he flashed a straight red card at Malen. The Roma striker lunged into a tackle after a heavy touch, but went over the ball and studs-up on Bruno Kaiki's ankle. It was clumsy more than malicious, but certainly high, late, and somewhat out of control.

ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Donyell Malen of AS Roma reacts after he receives a red card from referee Michael Fabbri during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and AS Roma at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Como nearly took advantage moments later, but Maxi Perrone ballooned over from 12 yards after Diao sent Wesley to ground, then Tasos Douvikas smashed his finish against the side-netting.

There was an odd situation on 67 minutes when referee Michael Fabbri sustained a knee injury, so had to exchange places with fourth official Simone Sozza for the final 20 minutes.

ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Referee Michael Fabbri receives medical treatment during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and AS Roma at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Gollini flew to palm a Nico Paz snapshot over the bar from the D, and rushed off his line again to deny the Argentina talent on a ball over the top.

Roma were under siege for the final stages, Mancini throwing himself in the way of a Trevoh Chalobah effort and Douvikas skimming the far post with an angled drive in stoppages.

articles.title: Vurt wants you to look at vertical videos as a genre of their own
articles.summary: Vurt is betting that the next big thing in vertical entertainment is living on wide-screen TVs.﻿
articles.body: From Disney Plus to HBO Max, almost every major established streaming service is experimenting with ways to get into vertical content. It’s clear that these companies see video-focused social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram as existential threats. In this arms race for viewers’ attention, it has often felt like everyone is trying to find new ways to exist on people’s phones. But a new startup thinks that the next step in vertical series’ evolution is going to take place on our wide-screen televisions. Unlike most vertical microdrama / series streaming platforms on the market that have focused on mobile viewing experiences, Vurt has been making a pivot into smart TVs. The company recently launched dedicated apps for Apple TV and Android TV that give users access to 3,500 episodes across more than 100 different shows. Since launching in March, Vurt’s userbase has grown from 10,000 to 675,000 users. Vurt primarily features the kind of soapy, melodramatic microdramas that have made rival services like DramaBox and ReelShort popular. But whereas those platforms have become inundated with AI-generated slop, the vast majority of Vurt’s series are produced with human casts and crews. And because Vurt monetizes its content through ad partnerships, viewers can watch all of it for free instead of dealing with convoluted microtransactions. [Media: When I spoke with Vurt cofounder / angel investor Hilmon Sorey this week, he told me that the company’s big push into dedicated TV apps was driven by direct feedback from users. People wanted a way to beam verticals they were already watching via their phones onto bigger screens, but Vurt’s development team thought that they could take things a step further. “At first, we first developed the ability for folks to cast to smart TVs,” Sorey said. “But we decided that wasn’t the best experience because we could leverage all of the technology in those large-screen devices to bring features like HD / 4K video, and the ability to do really high-quality audio.” To build out its library, Vurt signs licensing agreements with production studios and creators that gives them a 50/50 revenue split. Independent creators can directly submit their projects for distribution on the platform, and once approved, it can be available to stream in just a few days. Sorey said that being fair to creators and taking cues from them are core tenets of Vurt’s corporate philosophy. He also pointed to Vurt’s decision to rely on a “free-to-finish” model as the main way it works to be fair to its users. “If you are a platform that’s doing your own original content and you don’t have creators to pay, then ‘give us $20 and we’ll give you 500 coffee beans’ kind of gamification is intentional,” Sorey insisted. “It’s a ruse that they can use to boggle your mind because they control that entire content ecosystem.” Vurt’s foray onto televisions is coming at a time when more established vertical-focused platforms have been looking into ways to exist beyond people’s phones. This past June, Instagram beefed up its TV app to include Reels, disappearing Stories, and horizontally oriented videos — all of which felt like attempts at keeping pace with YouTube. Vurt told me that the company is staying focused on vertical content, but is currently developing new kinds of programming like original series and livestreamed sporting events. In the buildup to launching its TV apps, Vurt consulted content creators about how they like to watch films and TV shows. Many reported preferring viewing things in movie theaters or on big screens because of how immersive those experiences felt. But according to Sorey, the creators also insisted that vertical microdramas can feel just as engaging whether they’re watched on a phone with earbuds in or on a television screen. “You can have a different kind of immersive experience — even on a wide screen in vertical format — because verticals tell their stories in a very different way,” Sorey said. “You’ve got to have your hook to begin and at the tail end of that, you’ve got to thrust them into the next episode by virtue of a cliffhanger.” Sorey believes that the stylistic elements vertical microdramas have become known for — formulaic plots, questionable acting, and exceedingly short episodes — make them a specific kind of entertainment that’s distinct from traditional TV shows and films. Those qualities are what tend to make some people see vertical content as unwatchable, but they also seem to be part of what’s keeping Vurt’s users engaged. Sorey says that Vurt has seen overall engagement time increase for viewers using the company’s TV apps. That’s likely because those viewers have a convenient way to consume Vurt’s content without having to pick up their phones. Though a service like Vurt might make sense for people already hooked on microdramas, what’s far less clear is whether there’s really a broader appetite for vertical videos flanked by blank spaces. With so many other platforms experimenting with ways to turn everything into endless feeds of vertical videos, though, Vurt may be on to something.

articles.title: Elon Musk's mom Maye nearly turned down SI Swimsuit cover over 'wrinkles and cellulite'
articles.summary: Maye Musk nearly turned down her Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover over wrinkle fears, but a phone call from her daughter changed everything.
articles.body: Maye Musk nearly passed on the chance to make a splash in Sports Illustrated Swimsuit because she worried about looking "wrinkly" in the iconic magazine. The Canadian-born, South African-raised model made history in 2022 as the oldest Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover model at 74. Martha Stewart later broke the record at 81 in 2023. Now, Musk is looking back at the milestone and her journey from a single mother of three to a sought-after model in her new book, "Timeless." "At my age, you have wrinkles and cellulite on your arms and on your thighs, so I prefer to wear long sleeves," the mother of tech mogul Elon Musk told Fox News Digital. "So, the idea of wearing a swimsuit was very uncomfortable. But then my daughter called me. I told her they were going to be shooting in Belize. She instantly said, 'You've got to go. Belize is beautiful.' So, I did. I took a chance." MAYE MUSK DEFENDS SYDNEY SWEENEY'S NUDE SPORTS AD AND RECALLS 12-YEAR PATH TO CITIZENSHIP In the book, Musk wrote, "I was still 73. My skin showed the signs of my weight having cycled up and down so many times in my life, including for each of my pregnancies. I'm wrinkly and I have cellulite. Swimsuit model?" Despite her worries, Musk said she felt at ease when she began posing for photographer Yu Tsai. She even wore colorful two-pieces for the occasion. And I knew they're not going to publish ugly photos. At one point, I felt so at ease that I even started dancing with the local people. I was in awe of exploring a new country, a new culture. That's what I love doing. And I got to celebrate me." WATCH: MAYE MUSK DISCUSSES RAISING ELON MUSK, ESCAPING TOXIC MARRIAGE IN NEW MEMOIR ‘TIMELESS’ Looking back, Musk said she wonders why she was so nervous. "When women go to the beach, they wrap a towel around themselves," she said. "But men, they could be obese, and they're still strutting in Speedos with such confidence. We really have to make a change. And if any man insults your body, well, they can get lost. There's always going to be somebody who feels the need to trash on you. It's not fair. But it's all about embracing who you are and not apologizing for that." Musk didn't undergo a makeover to appear younger for the cover. Her signature silver hair remained untouched. "Why do I need to color my hair?" Musk said. "You have to do the roots every four weeks, and I used to do them myself. Your hair then becomes very brittle because it's so damaged. And it grows out. And then I decided to cut my hair short. Soon after, I had four billboards in Times Square. I didn't feel like a granny. I felt fashionable." It wasn't the first time Musk took a chance on a modeling gig. In her book, Musk describes a phone call she received from her agent: "Tomorrow, you pose naked for the cover of TIME magazine. You're the only model they want and they won't budge." Musk had never done a nude shoot because, as she wrote, "nobody had ever asked." "I picked up the phone to dial Elon first, then stopped myself," Musk wrote. "I already knew what he would say: 'Absolutely not.' He was not the kind of son who wanted his mother naked on magazine covers. Not prudish, but definitely more conservative when it came to nudity. So I called Tosca. I wasn't too surprised to find that she was not in love with the idea, either. 'You never do naked!' she said. Her instinct was protective, not wanting me to risk an uncomfortable experience." "Finally, I called Kimbal," she wrote. "Of my three children, he is the most relaxed and free-spirited. (He met his current wife at Burning Man.) He had a completely different perspective. ‘It’s TIME magazine. It’s journalism,’ he said. ‘Not some nudie magazine. It’ll be tasteful. You have nothing to worry about. Do it.’" Musk told Fox News Digital it was important for her to get her children's approval before posing nude. "Well, would you want your mother naked on the front cover of a magazine?" she said. "But it was Kimbal who encouraged me. He said it would be tasteful. He's always been a free spirit. And I trust him. When I arrived for the photoshoot, they were very careful with me. You have a makeup artist who has to go through your whole body. Then they did my hair and very plain makeup. Then they sat me with a mirror in front of me, so I could see exactly what the photographer sees." "The photographer came in for the shoot, and maybe five minutes later, it was over," she said. "It was really quick and very respectful. They immediately brought a robe for me. I got changed and went home. That's all there was to it." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? The longtime dietitian also believes that taking care of your health plays an important role in feeling your best at any age. "It gets harder to lose weight as you get older," Musk said. "With my patients, I always tell them to plan ahead. If you get hungry, there's no salad next to you. There's a donut. Also, only eat when you're hungry. And when you are hungry, make sure there is healthy food around, no desserts or chocolates. And if my patient didn't take the journey seriously, I would tell them, 'You can't come anymore.'" "Even 10 pounds can make you feel uncomfortable," she said. "Everything is tight and you don't have confidence. You have to track your food intake. If a patient goes off what I recommended, they need to explain why. You need to hold yourself accountable if you want to make smarter choices for your health." Musk said each decade of her life has been better than the last. At 78, she's happily embracing aging and hopes other women will do the same. When she was nearing 90, her hands weren't strong enough to do the wood carvings she loved. So, by 94, she started doing computer art. My older sister taught her. She died at 98. But she always remained curious and busy. She was always exploring." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "You're never too old to start again," Musk said. "And don't worry about the wrinkles. A man doesn't care if he gets wrinkles. He still has his confidence. When you get insecure, you become less attractive. I didn't do anything to my face because I wanted to frown and have expression. But also, don't mix with people who make you feel insecure. They're not your friends. And there will be people who will push you down. You can't stay down. A Brooklyn specialty store is facing heat after singer and talk show host Kelly Clarkson called it out in a scathing post shared online. Clarkson, known for winning "American Idol" and later starring in shows like "The Voice" and "The Kelly Clarkson Show," claimed a store employee treated her poorly and assumed she couldn't afford the store's products. The 44-year-old's post has since gone viral, prompting her fans and netizens alike to flood the store's social media pages with critical messages. The heat, apparently, has been too much for the New York store to bear, considering they've disabled all comments.

"Wow, dude," she continued before calling the store employee an "idiot" who "lost a huge sale."

Clarkson's post has since been seen by 22 million people, prompting a flurry of responses from users who had her back.

One user slammed the store for allegedly failing to "treat everyone with respect and kindness," while another user said it's wrong for store employees to assume what a customer can or cannot afford.

Other X users also posted screenshots of their negative Google reviews, including one showing the company's five-star rating plummeting to 3.6 stars.

Critical reactions weren't limited to X or Google, either. On Instagram , reactions were much the same, if not worse, prompting Art of Play to disable users' ability to comment.

According to Page Six , the New York specialty store declined to comment when asked about the alleged interaction.

Kelly Clarkson Isn't The Only Celebrity Who Has Allegedly Been Treated Poorly At Stores

Bethenny Frankel from "The Real Housewives of New York City" shared a similar experience years ago, telling her social media followers that she was stopped from entering a Chanel store in Chicago.

Like Clarkson, the reality star and Skinny Girl business owner, who's reportedly worth $80 million, said that when she tried to shop, the doorman, whom she described as Lurch in "The Addams Family," told her she needed a prior appointment to enter.

"That's beside the point," she said. "I was straight off a plane in sweathy tshirt and not dolled up or looking wealthy. There are several ways to convey a message and this way was rudeness and elitist and exclusionary, which is also a crime."

Frankel continued, "In business, first impressions are lasting. I would never want anyone to feel lesser than, particularly from a luxury brand making billions off of people buying into the hype." She finished by encouraging business owners and employees to be kind to customers of all "socioeconomic backgrounds," calling it "timeless and classic."

articles.body: Paramore frontwoman Hayley Williams fired back at the Department of Homeland Security on Monday with a vulgar message after the agency defended federal immigration officers, following the singer's anti-ICE outburst at a concert in Chula Vista, California. Williams posted a screenshot to her Instagram Story, along with a profanity-laced insult after the agency suggested she thank federal law enforcement officers rather than criticize their service. "And may I suggest all Nazi b------ suck on my fat d---," Williams said in response to DHS, according to Rolling Stone. "America is grateful all the time for our federal law enforcement officers who keep us safe," the spokesperson told Fox News Digital at the time. Christianity sees all people as made in the image of God, so are all valuable, no matter how successful, and puts self-sacrifice above power," she added.Williams has previously used major concert appearances to deliver political messages. During Paramore's performance at the 2024 iHeartRadio Music Festival, she urged Americans to vote against Trump, criticizing his political agenda and warning about the country's democratic future.Williams' latest remarks also came as DHS reported an increase in assaults against immigration officers. articles.title: 'Reagan' star Lesley-Anne Down relives 3 terrifying brushes with death: ‘I should have been killed’
articles.summary: Lesley-Anne Down recalls three harrowing brushes with danger, including a chilling link to the Moors murders and a terrifying fake taxi escape.
articles.body: Lesley-Anne Down believes she's already used up three of her nine lives. The actress, who takes on the Iron Lady opposite Dennis Quaid in "Reagan," has shown plenty of steel off-screen, recalling "three times in my life when I should have been killed by other people." For Down, known for her roles in "North and South" and "Upstairs, Downstairs," the unsettling experiences began when she was just 10 years old. MORGAN FAIRCHILD SAYS TWO MEN ONCE ABDUCTED HER OFF NYC STREET AS BYSTANDERS LAUGHED "I remember there was a little girl, one of a number of children who were murdered and buried on the moors in England," the British star told Fox News Digital. "There was a little girl who had dark hair and blue eyes and was my age, 10. Her name was Leslie Ann Downey. My mother got phone calls when this little girl's identity was announced." "It wasn't me, of course," said Down. "But it certainly freaked her out. Leslie Ann Downey was about six months younger than me. It turned out there were two people, a man and a woman. Ian Brady and Myra Hindley. They were the killers." Brady and Hindley murdered five children between 1963 and 1965, with several of their victims buried on Saddleworth Moor in northern England, according to The Associated Press. The case became known as the Moors murders. The five victims were Downey, Pauline Reade, John Kilbride, Keith Bennett and Edward Evans, who ranged in age from 10 to 17. Bennett's body has never been found. According to accounts of the case, Downey was abducted after Hindley asked her to help carry packages to a car. Hindley died in 2002 while serving a life sentence. Brady died in a psychiatric hospital in 2017. The case frightened Down’s family. But it wouldn’t be the last time danger came close to home. "A year later, my mother and I were coming back from the launderette with the washing," Down said. "I ran ahead. I left the washing, I left my mother and just ran ahead. I ran uphill and then over a footbridge. As I ran over the footbridge, a man came from the other side. He's walking towards me. He stops in the middle of the footbridge and says, 'Hello.' He then was going to put me in his car." "He told me he needed a babysitter, and he would call my parents when we got to his house," Down said. "I remember having one foot in the car. Seeing my mother broke the spell. Then he was gone. But I still remember that horrible feeling swooping in before my mother came." But when a car pulled up in the countryside, she climbed in and quickly noticed something was wrong. "As soon as he's driving away, I'm already feeling that horrible feeling," Down said. "I looked around and there were no radios or anything, like a taxi is supposed to have. So I said, 'Could you pull over, please?' He said, 'Oh no, we don't need to pull over. We'll be there soon.'" Down said she decided to jump from the moving car. "I opened the door and threw myself out of the 25-mile an hour car," she said. "I fell onto the curb in a puddle. I was covered in blood. There was nobody around. What did he do? He pulled the car door shut and drove off at top speed. I didn't freeze up because I couldn't. That feeling was familiar to me. I've been through it." Down, now 72, earned a Golden Globe nomination for her role opposite Patrick Swayze in "North and South." articles.title: George A. Romero’s Season of the Witch is a slow-burn feminist occult drama
articles.summary: After inventing the modern zombie, Romero made a feminist film about a suffering house wife turning to witchcraft.
articles.body: George A. Romero is obviously best known as the father of the modern zombie movie. But between inventing the genre with Night of the Living Dead and his outbreak horror, The Crazies, Romero made two much lesser-known films: There’s Always Vanilla, which I’ll admit I’ve never seen, and Season of the Witch, or, as it was originally titled, Hungry Wives. Hungry Wives was supposed to be an exploitation film. The studio marketed it as a softcore porn, but it failed to find an audience — probably because the movie features minimal nudity, just one sex scene, and lots of talking. It was an undeniable flop upon its release in 1973. It was eventually rereleased as Season of the Witch after Romero’s Dawn of the Dead sparked renewed interest in his work. While sadly, Romero’s original 130 minute cut of the film has been lost, parts of it have been recovered and restored, expanding the 89 minute original release to 104 minutes. An obvious reason for its failure, beyond the distributor butchering it it by cutting 40 minutes, is that, what Romero made wasn’t a softcore porn, instead it’s a slow-burn feminist drama where the occult is almost incidental. Protaganist Joan Mitchell is trapped in an abussive marriage and unhappy with her role as submissive housewife. She eventually turns from therapy, to witchcraft in an attempt to escape her humdrum life. Season of the Witch has its issues, for sure. The production value is quite low — apparently the movie was made for just $100,000 (around $800,000 adjusted for inflation). The acting is also wildly uneven. While star Jan White turns in an excellent performance, others appear to be reading off cue cards or chew scenery with Pachino-levels of camp. Still, there’s something compelling about Romero’s directing and his, for the time, boldly progressive take on feminism. For all of its reliance on dialogue over action, Season of the Witch still manages a tense and, at times, halucinatory atmosphere. And it all leads to a somewhat predictable, but still extremely satisfying ending. Season of the Wich is available to stream on Mubi and Kanopy.

articles.title: Kid Rock details unlikely Eminem collaboration on new Christian album
articles.summary: Kid Rock says he didn't want to allow political differences to stand in the way of collaborating with longtime friend Eminem on his new faith-inspired album "Halfway 2 Jesus."
articles.body: Kid Rock opened up about his collaboration with fellow Detroit musician Eminem on his new Christian album, "Halfway 2 Jesus," telling "My View with Lara Trump" on Saturday that the longtime friends have refused to let their political differences come between them. The rocker said he hoped the collaboration would send a message about maintaining friendships despite political disagreements, highlighting his nearly 40-year friendship with Eminem. "We said years ago, we said, 'Man, let's not let politics divide us.' And we never did. And so when I asked him to be part of this... he totally got it," Kid Rock said. "Two little foul-mouthed white rappers from Detroit maybe could set a good example for the rest of this country" by showing that it's OK to differ politically and still be friends, he added. PRESIDENT TALKS 'TRUMP OCEAN,' TRADES JOKES WITH TENNESSEE CROWD AS KID ROCK KICKS OFF SPRAWLING RALLY He called Eminem a "class act" and said the freedom to hold differing opinions is what makes the United States great. "Since when can you not express your points and your views and your opinions?" Kid Rock said, adding that he believes politics has no place onstage. Instead, the Detroit-born singer hopes to use his music to bring people together through faith. His new Christian album reflects his lifelong relationship with God, he said, rather than a sudden religious conversion. He described the album as a collection of songs centered on forgiveness and second chances and outlined plans to bring Christian revival-style performances to arenas and stadiums. "After Charlie Kirk was assassinated, like a lot of people, I started to become closer to my faith," Kid Rock said, adding that his renewed focus on faith inspired a period of songwriting that shaped the album. GRANGER SMITH SAYS FAME CAN BECOME ‘POISON’ AFTER LEAVING COUNTRY MUSIC FOR MINISTRY Despite the album's religious themes, the singer rejected the suggestion that he had undergone a sudden religious conversion, saying his faith has always been part of his identity. "I didn't get saved. I'm still Kid Rock. I'm still going to drink a beer and smoke a cigar," he said. "I feel like I've always been right with God." Kid Rock also pointed to a connection between his birthday, Jan. 17, 1971, and his middle name, James, and the Bible verse James 1:17, which he said "basically says all good things come from God." WHY ERIKA KIRK’S FORGIVENESS MATTERS Beyond his personal faith, the singer said he hopes the album will encourage Americans to put aside their political differences. "This record is about second chances and forgiveness. It's about trying to heal some of the division in our country," he said. He said he wants to bring his Christian music to arenas and stadiums, combining a traditional rock concert with a religious revival. "And I want to have revivals, Saturday night revivals in arenas, stadiums, people drinking beer, having a good time, celebrating our Lord and Savior," he said, calling the proposed performances a "full-on monster rock show." "I think that could do a lot of good in the world."

articles.title: Tragedia en el festival EDC de Medellín: reportan la muerte de un turista extranjero en la primera jornada
articles.standfirst: Murió extranjero durante el festival de música EDC en el Atanasio Girardot de Medellín: esto se sabe
articles.summary: Murió extranjero durante el festival de música EDC en el Atanasio Girardot de Medellín: esto se sabe
articles.body: La primera edición en Medellín del festival de música electrónica Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC) se vio empañada por la muerte de un asistente extranjero durante la jornada inaugural del evento, llevado a cabo en la Unidad Deportiva Atanasio Girardot. La víctima fue identificada como Ismael Gerardo Méndez Huertas, de 27 años y de nacionalidad costarricense. Según los reportes preliminares de la Policía Metropolitana y los equipos médicos del evento, el joven fue hallado inconsciente y con marcadas dificultades respiratorias en uno de los baños del complejo deportivo durante la madrugada. Méndez Huertas recibió la atención médica inicial por parte de las cuadrillas de primeros auxilios del festival y posteriormente fue trasladado de urgencia en ambulancia al Hospital Pablo Tobón Uribe. A pesar de las maniobras de reanimación y los esfuerzos del personal asistencial, se confirmó su deceso al poco tiempo de ingresar al centro médico. Las autoridades judiciales de Medellín y el Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal iniciaron las investigaciones correspondientes para esclarecer la causa exacta del fallecimiento. Entre las principales hipótesis bajo evaluación se encuentra una posible sobredosis o intoxicación por sustancias estupefacientes, aunque no se descarta ninguna otra causa médica hasta que se conozca el dictamen forense definitivo. Así mismo, las autoridades locales adelantan los trámites consulares con la embajada de Costa Rica para gestionar la entrega y repatriación del cuerpo a su país de origen.

articles.title: 'Dizzy' Lazio join Inter at top of Serie A as Roma and AC Milan held
articles.summary: Lazio moved level on points with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday as pursuers Roma and AC Milan were both held.AC Milan...
articles.body:
Lazio moved level on points with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday as pursuers Roma and AC Milan were both held.

Ten-man Roma could not keep pace as Donyell Malen's red card overshadowed a 0-0 stalemate in Como to sit two points behind with leaders in third.

AC Milan were held 1-1 at Sassuolo to leave them four points adrift of the leaders in fourth.

Under Gennaro Gattuso, who has bounced back after his failure at the helm of the Italian national side who missed out on the 2026 World Cup, Lazio continued their strong start to the season.

Still unbeaten, the Roman outfit secured a fifth victory in six matches to pull level on 16 points with Inter Milan, who beat Parma 3–0 at the San Siro on Saturday.

"We can't look at the standings, otherwise we will get dizzy. We have to take it day by day," said Gattuso.

Their run comes despite ongoing fan protests against owner Claudio Lotito that have left Lazio's home matches sparsely attended amid a stadium boycott.

Nuno Tavares gave Lazio a third-minute lead and Gustav Isaksen doubled it midway through the first half.

Monza had Lorenzo Lucchesi sent off on 35 minutes for hauling down Tijjani Noslin as he broke through on goal, but the 16th-placed visitors rattled Lazio after the break, pulling a goal back and coming close to equalising before conceding a third goal in the closing stages.

Ruben Amorim's Milan maintained their unbeaten start but drew for the third time in their last four league games.

Matteo Gabbia went off injured early on with the breakthrough not coming until the 63rd minute when Luka Modric slipped in Adrien Rabiot to fire home a powerful finish.

Sassuolo responded immediately as Mike Maignan was forced into a double save, and the Rossoneri's lead lasted just five minutes before substitute Cas Odenthal turned in the equaliser in a crowded box from a corner.

Roma continued their unbeaten start against Como but could only pick up a point in the first goalless draw of the Serie A season.

The dismissal of league top scorer Malen for a dangerous tackle early in the second half forced Roma to scale back their ambitions after a bright start.

Neither team could find the breakthrough in a clash between two sides widely regarded as dark horses for the title.

"We played two thirds of the match a man down, that is the disappointing thing," Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini told DAZN.

"We were confident we had an excellent chance, but we were forced to defend with 10 men, and we did so with order and clarity. When you play 30 minutes with 10 men and come away with a draw, that is fine."

Roma had the better of the first half as Lorenzo Pellegrini, making his first league start in six months, curled a shot off the post after Paulo Dybala's weak finish failed to trouble Jean Butez.

But Malen's reckless lunge eight minutes into the second half proved costly as the Roma striker, who has scored six league goals this season, was shown a straight red card.

Como were unable to find a way past Pierluigi Gollini as the Roma goalkeeper kept a clean sheet on his first league appearance for more than two years following an injury to first-choice Mile Svilar.

Both sides are in Champions League action on Wednesday, when Roma host Real Madrid at the Stadio Olimpico and Como travel to Feyenoord.

Bologna picked up their first win of the season by beating Lecce 2-1.
